title: Shared hooks must distinguish inactive installs from failures
body: Shared configuration is not local activation. Missing Mason and a checkout without local hook setup must stay quiet; corrupt setup and failed active checks remain visible. A PATH guard handles only an absent executable. The earlier strict managed MCP launch made fresh clones disconnect before explaining setup. MCP should serve context and explain the missing setup without creating local activation or authorizing hooks. Each checkout still runs setup explicitly. Resolve managed hooks from the event payload before checking local setup: the launch cwd can be outside the repo or belong to the original checkout. Claude's CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR stays at that original checkout after entering a worktree. An outside-Git fallback is safe only with an unambiguous checkout; conflicting roots or multiple worktrees remain unknown. Preserve pre-edit coverage for shell and unknown tools. Read-only observations must not advance audit freshness or imply a passing check. Configuration, observed activation, and verification remain separate. These are proposed constraints supported by isolated regressions, not an independently accepted policy or proof of every host configuration.

content.title: Shared hooks must distinguish inactive installs from failures
content.body: A shared hook configuration does not establish that each developer has installed Mason or initialized the current checkout. In an isolated 0.16.1 reproduction on 2026-09-09, the generated command with Mason absent from PATH exited 127; with Mason installed but no local setup receipt it exited 0 while emitting a setup warning on every invocation. A PATH-only guard addresses only the first case. Proposed behavior: inactive integrations should avoid repeated warnings, while an active integration must still report failed evidence capture and unknown verification. Setup, status, and teardown should own this behavior consistently. Preserve pre-edit coverage for shell and unknown tools when reducing hook overhead; editor-only or post-only matching loses that coverage. This proposal records reproduced behavior and recommended constraints, not an implemented fix or approved design.
